stem: An adult client's serum sodium is 122 mmol/L. How should the nurse interpret this result?

options.A: The value represents hypernatremia because it is above the adult sodium reference interval and suggests excess extracellular sodium.
options.B: The value represents hyponatremia and requires clinical assessment, including attention to symptoms and the acuity of the sodium decline.
options.C: The value falls within the expected adult sodium reference interval and does not represent a clinically meaningful sodium abnormality.
options.D: The value is mildly elevated rather than low, so neurologic assessment and evaluation of fluid or electrolyte status are not indicated.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance gives a serum sodium reference interval of 135–145 mmol/L for patients age 1 year and older. A sodium of 122 mmol/L is therefore hyponatremia. Mayo notes that symptoms of hyponatremia result from brain swelling and that clinical manifestations depend primarily on the rate of change in sodium concentration rather than only the absolute value. Therefore B is correct; A and D reverse the abnormality and C incorrectly calls the result normal.
educational_objective: Recognize a serum sodium of 122 mmol/L as hyponatremia requiring further clinical assessment, including neurologic status and acuity of onset.
source_version_date: Current Mayo test catalog; test-definition document generated May 31, 2026; live Mayo resources retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Reference Values: age ≥1 year 135–145 mmol/L. Clinical Information: hyponatremia symptoms reflect brain swelling. Interpretation: symptoms depend primarily on rate of change in sodium concentration rather than absolute concentration alone.
source_claim_supported: A sodium of 122 mmol/L is below the adult reference interval and is hyponatremia; clinical severity depends importantly on symptoms and rate of decline.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor and interpret diagnostic/laboratory findings and changes in condition.
correction_summary: Balanced all options as complete sodium interpretations while preserving the current reference interval and clinically appropriate contextual assessment.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — Mayo's 135–145 mmol/L reference interval makes 122 unambiguously low, and Mayo explicitly emphasizes rate-of-change-dependent manifestations.
